issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int in SealSaloon, but the solution implements a static method named computeMealCost(Meal) instead. The template Main (commented) also calls computeMealCost, while the solution Main (commented) refers to calculateTotalPrice. This name mismatch across artifacts creates confusion about the expected API and could cause students or tests to look for the wrong method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's computeMealCost method to calculateTotalPrice with the signature public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal), and update any calls in Main and the template to use calculateTotalPrice. Ensure the problem statement, template, and solution consistently reference calculateTotalPrice.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's cost, but the template and solution artifacts use a different identifier computeMealCost in some places. Specifically, the template Main references shop.computeMealCost(...), the SealSaloon implementation defines computeMealCost(...), while the solution Main calls calculateTotalPrice(...). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (computing the total price of a Meal) creates confusion for students about which method to implement and which name to call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the meal cost method across all artifacts. Rename computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice in SealSaloon (keeping it static) and update all calls in Main and template code to shop.calculateTotalPrice(...) so they match the problem statement.
